proof_attempt_summary: D0 developed a density-free signed primitive, matched minimax estimation and honest expected-length rate arguments, and a conservative interval, then repaired the joint visit/measurement sampling law and removed unnecessary global class restrictions. D0.5 still found the conditional rare-interval functional CLT and its three argmin limits unproved; the current note must not be cited as a sound proof of those results. tldr: A density-free signed primitive reveals two local information channels for the first threshold crossing of a monotone treatment-effect curve in a randomized repeated-outcome trial: rare conditionally independent visit--error draws and the average latent subject trajectory shared across visits. Over the broadened shape class, whose uniform results require neither global arm-mean Lipschitzness nor global trajectory \(2+\eta\) moments, the estimator and a conservative regime-adaptive interval attain the matched minimax estimation and honest expected-length rate \((nm)^{-1/3}\vee n^{-1/2}\). Local continuity and local moment assumptions are used only for the Chernoff, Chernoff--Gaussian convolution, and Gaussian objective and argmin laws. These are not claims of full experiment equivalence or semiparametric efficiency.
gap: Kim and Zhao (2013), pp. 203--206, model (2), equations (7)--(11), and Theorem 1, with Theorem 2 on p. 207, study a local-kernel estimator of a longitudinal mean curve and obtain a self-normalized Gaussian central limit theorem with visit-level and within-subject variance channels. Their target is the mean curve, their regularity and sparse-to-dense classification are tied to smoothing and bandwidth, and they do not study a monotone threshold onset or an inverse argmin. The present theorem targets the onset \(t_0\) through an unsmoothed integrated primitive, assumes monotonicity and a two-sided crossing margin without a uniform higher-derivative modulus, and claims a cube-root-to-Gaussian transition at \(m\asymp\sqrt n\). Chen, Gao, Fu, and Zhu (2019) provide the closest smoothed longitudinal inverse comparison, while published isotonic local-limit theory treats independent observations or dependence along one sequence; none of these inspected results supplies the combined growing-cluster onset law, matched onset risk, and honest expected-length frontier.
